summary: test-account-portal-fe postinstall exfiltrates host identifiers via DNS OAST beacon and prebuilt native addon POST to bare-IP C2
details: test-account-portal-fe@100.100.102 ships an empty index.js (module.exports = {}) and a postinstall script that performs two install-time exfiltration actions. First, postinstall.js constructs the subdomain <hostname>.<package>.db4jlbku53082dmp0d7g3mffj7s7aordk.oast.me and triggers DNS resolution for it, leaking the installer's hostname and package context to an interactsh/OAST callback domain. Second, postinstall.js require()s prebuilds/linux-x64/addon.node, a prebuilt ELF for which no source is shipped; the addon reads gethostname, getpwuid (uid/username), and the npm_package_name and npm_config_registry environment variables, and POSTs them as form data (h=&u=&p=&r=) to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://64.181.165.115/dc. The package version (100.100.102) and the empty library surface are consistent with a dependency-confusion / name-squat lure whose sole purpose is the install-time beacon and native dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
